title: My alarm is too quiet
body:
If your alarm is too quiet, you may simply need to adjust the volume. If it's still too quiet after that, another setting may be affecting it.

First, adjust the volume in your iPhone's Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Ringtone and Alerts. This controls the volume of the alarm while your iPhone is locked.

Second, adjust the volume in the Lasso app itself. Open Lasso's Settings > Volume. This controls the volume after you've responded to the alert on your Lock Screen. Match the volume in both places for a seamless transition.

Third, confirm whether Lasso's Gradual Wake Up feature is enabled by going to Lasso's Settings > Wake Up and checking whether 'Instant' or 'Gradual' is selected. 'Gradual' will make the alarm start very quiet and slowly increase to your set volume.

If the alarm is still quiet, you can try experimenting with the following settings. Change with Buttons: If 'Change with Buttons' is enabled in your iPhone's Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Ringtone and Alerts, it's easy to accidentally lower the volume of the alarm. Attention Aware Features: If 'Attention Aware Features' is toggled on in your iPhone's Settings > Face ID & Passcode, the alarm volume may be lowered, but only while your iPhone is unlocked and you are looking at the screen. Limit Maximum Volume: If 'Limit Maximum Volume' is enabled in your iPhone's Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Volume Limit, it could be reducing the volume of the alarm after you've unlocked your iPhone. However, this should not affect the volume while the iPhone is locked. Reduce Loud Sounds: If 'Reduce Loud Sounds' is enabled in your iPhone's Settings > Sounds & Haptics, it could be reducing the volume of the alarm after you've unlocked your iPhone. However, this should not affect the alarm volume while your iPhone is locked.
